newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dlr opens firmer after Australian rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Canada dlr opens firmer after Australian rate cut.

text.p: * Canada's dollar opened firmer on Wednesday at C$1.3835 (US$0.7228) lifted by interest to buy on the back of Australia's fifth rate cut in a year, dealers said. * They said talk of Aussie sales for Canada overnight drove Canada a bit stronger until some Canadian corporate interest to buy Aussie for Canada surfaced late in Asian trade.
In a surprise move on Wednesday the Reserve Bank of Australia cut its official cash rate by half a percentage point to 5.0 percent.
Analysts said the move caught the market off-guard because the cut was widely expected, but not before the Australian central bank's board meeting on August 5.

Dealers said they do not expect much more activity in the Canadian dollar as a result of the Australian rate cut, but that Canada's currency will likely trade in a slightly firmer range ahead of Statistics Canada's report on the nation's May gross domestic product on Friday.
A Reuters survey of economists forecast May GDP rose 0.3 percent on a monthly basis from 0.8 percent in April.
On the crosses, Canada's dollar rose to 1.3323 marks from Tuesday's close of 1.3263 marks and rose to 85.91 yen from Monday's 85.44 yen close.
